name: Apulum
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Legionary fortress of XIII Gemina and the province's administrative centre. The point is the modern settlement's reference location carried from the CND place record, not an excavated centroid.

name: Napoca
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Municipium and later colonia on the road north. Point carried from the CND place record.

name: Potaissa
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Legionary fortress of V Macedonica from c. 168. Point carried from the CND place record.

name: Porolissum
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The northern frontier command. The CND record carries an editorial reconstruction of the site position, and that provenance is carried through rather than upgraded here.

name: Colonia Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The provincial capital, forty kilometres from the Dacian royal seat whose name it took.

name: Tibiscum
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Road junction where the Lederata and Dierna approaches meet.

name: Micia
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Auxiliary fort and customs station on the Mureș.

name: Ampelum
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Seat of the procurator aurariarum, the gold-mining administration.

name: Resculum
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Fort at Bologa guarding the Criș approach. The ancient name attached to this fort is not settled, which is why the confidence is low.

name: Arcidava
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: First station on the Lederata road, at Vărădia.

name: Drobeta
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The bridgehead of Trajan's bridge, and the one site here whose position is fixed by standing remains.

name: Dierna
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: Danube crossing at Orșova; the modern town sits over it.

name: Romula
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: Principal town of the Olt corridor, behind the limes Alutanus.

name: Sucidava
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: Danube crossing at the mouth of the Olt, and the last Roman position held here into the sixth century.

name: Lederata road
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21; Tabula Peutingeriana segm. VI-VII
notes: One of the two invasion routes of 101-106 and a road of the Peutinger table. The drawn line joins attested stations in order; it is not a surveyed alignment and the intermediate stations are not plotted.

name: The imperial road
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The province's spine, from the capital to the northern command. The line joins attested stations in order and generalises every bend of the Mureș and Someș valleys it actually followed.

name: The Mureș valley road
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The customs road down the Mureș. Two stations only, so the drawn segment is a direction rather than a route.

name: The Danube bank road
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: The river road along the left bank. Drawn straight between crossings; the actual road follows the river, which this line does not.

name: The Olt corridor road
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: The road up the Olt behind the limes Alutanus, from the Danube crossing to the corridor's principal town.

name: The Resculum road
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: West from Napoca to the fort at Bologa and the passes beyond.

name: Limes Porolissensis
citation: Talbert (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), map 21
notes: The north-western frontier system of forts, towers and earthworks. The line is a schematic corridor drawn to show where the frontier ran, not a mapped earthwork: no segment here has been digitised from a survey.

name: Limes Alutanus
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: The Olt line, from the Danube to the Turnu Roșu pass. Schematic corridor, following the river's general course rather than any surveyed work.

name: Limes Transalutanus
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-35: Romula, Durostorum, Tomis (1969)
notes: The forward line east of the Olt, abandoned in the mid-third century before the province itself was. Schematic corridor; its end date is earlier than the province's and is the reason this layer is filtered per feature rather than as a block.
